2027-03-29.title: Monday within the Octave of Easter
readings: This Jesus God raised up, and of that all of us are witnesses
Keep me safe, O God; you are my hope (or: Alleluia)
Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me
2027-03-29.alt: Day within the Octave of Easter, kept with the rank of a solemnity. The Gloria is sung; the Easter Sequence may be sung before the Gospel acclamation; the dismissal has the double Alleluia. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-03-29.verse: Suddenly Jesus met them and said, “Greetings!” And they came to him, took hold of his feet, and worshiped him. Then Jesus said to them, “Do not be afraid; go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me.”
theo: The Church does not celebrate Easter for one day only. For eight days, the Octave, she lives each day as if it were Easter Sunday: the Gloria is sung, the Alleluia rings out, and each day's readings show us a new appearance of the risen Lord. The early Christians called this week the week of the white garments, because the newly baptized wore their white robes every day until the following Sunday. Today Peter stands up on the day of Pentecost with the Eleven and speaks to the crowd in Jerusalem. He speaks of “Jesus of Nazareth, a man attested to you by God with deeds of power, wonders, and signs.” He was handed over and crucified, “But God raised him up, having freed him from death, because it was impossible for him to be held in its power.” Then Peter reads Psalm 16, today's Psalm, as a prophecy: David sang, “you do not give me up to Sheol, or let your faithful one see the Pit.” But David died and was buried, and his tomb is still there. So he was speaking of the Messiah. “This Jesus God raised up, and of that all of us are witnesses.”

Notice what has happened to Peter. A few weeks earlier he was so afraid that he denied Jesus before a servant girl. Now he stands before thousands and speaks with boldness. Nothing explains that change except what he says: he has seen the Lord alive, and he has received the Holy Spirit. The Resurrection is not only proven by an empty tomb; it is proven by transformed lives. Peter's courage, the joy of the martyrs, the faith that spread to the ends of the earth, including the shores of Kerala, all flow from that first morning. The Psalm gives words to this new confidence: “I keep the LORD always before me; because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved. Therefore my heart is glad, and my soul rejoices; my body also rests secure.”

In the Gospel the women leave the tomb “quickly with fear and great joy” and run to tell the disciples. Fear and joy together: that is often how Easter faith begins. And on the way, “suddenly Jesus met them.” He greets them simply, as a friend would. They take hold of his feet, real feet, and worship him. He says: “Do not be afraid; go and tell my brothers.” He calls the disciples who abandoned him “my brothers.” The Resurrection is reconciliation. Matthew then tells of a different response. Some of the guards report to the chief priests, who pay them to say that the disciples stole the body while they were asleep. Matthew records this because, in his own time, this story was circulating as an explanation of the empty tomb. It is not a judgement on the Jewish people; it is a reminder that every age offers its own ways of explaining the Resurrection away. St Augustine asked with a smile: if the guards were asleep, how did they know who took the body? The truth cannot be bought. The empty tomb stands, the witnesses speak, and the Lord meets us still on the road with his greeting: do not be afraid.
conn: The eight days from Easter Sunday to the Second Sunday of Easter are celebrated as one great day. Each day ranks as a solemnity; no memorials of saints are kept.
The newly baptized wore their white garments all week and laid them aside on the following Sunday, once called “Sunday in white” (Dominica in albis).
Acts places this speech on the day of Pentecost. The Church reads it in the Easter Octave because it is the first public proclamation of the Resurrection.
Peter points out that David's tomb was still known in Jerusalem (Acts 2:29). Psalm 16 could not be fully true of David; it is fulfilled in the Messiah, whose body did not see corruption.
Matthew 28:8. Holy fear before the power of God, and overflowing joy at the good news: the right response to Easter.
For the first time in Matthew, Jesus calls the disciples his brothers (Matthew 28:10). The risen Lord restores the friendship they had broken.
Matthew 28:11–15 answers a rumour of his own day. The Church reads it without hostility to the Jewish people (Nostra Aetate 4).
Where the call began. The risen Lord sends his disciples back to the place of their first love, to begin again.
altar: The women took hold of the feet of the risen Jesus. At the altar we receive the same risen Lord, not as a memory but as a living presence, in his true Body and Blood.
Today's collect prays that we may hold fast in our lives to the Sacrament we received in faith. Each Communion is a meeting on the road with the One who says: do not be afraid.

live: Tell one person today, simply, that Christ is risen and what that means for you.
Begin each day of this Octave with a short prayer: “Lord, I keep you always before me.”
Like Jesus who called the disciples “my brothers,” reach out to someone you have drifted from.
Pray each day this week for those baptized at Easter, that they may hold fast to the faith.
fathers: The guards were told to say that the disciples stole the body while they slept. O wretched cunning! You bring forward sleeping witnesses. If they were asleep, what could they see? If they saw nothing, what is their testimony worth?
The days between the Resurrection and the Ascension were not spent idly: in them great mysteries were confirmed and great truths revealed, so that our faith might rest on certainty and not on fear.
The women run, carrying the joy of the Resurrection. The Lord meets them on the way and greets them, so that the mouth of woman, through which death once entered, might now announce life.
magis: The appearances of the risen Christ and the testimony of the witnesses.
Christ was not abandoned to the realm of the dead; his body did not see corruption (Acts 2:27).
Sunday, the day of the Resurrection, and the Easter Octave.
The laity as witnesses to the Resurrection, proclaiming Christ by the testimony of their lives.
Scripture is not to be read so as to blame the Jewish people.
saints: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, Salome, Joanna and the other women who followed Jesus from Galilee were the first witnesses of the empty tomb and the first to meet the risen Lord.

The Octave of Easter continues until Sunday 4 April, Divine Mercy Sunday. 2 Apr (St Francis of Paola) and other memorials are not kept during the Octave. 5 Apr: the Annunciation of the Lord (transferred).
2027-03-29.prayer: O God, who give constant increase to your Church by new offspring, grant that your servants may hold fast in their lives to the Sacrament they have received in faith. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Risen Lord Jesus, you met the women on the road and said: do not be afraid. Meet us today on our roads. Turn our fear into joy, make us bold witnesses like Peter, and call back to you all our brothers and sisters who have wandered away. Alleluia. Amen.

Sunday and the joy of the Resurrection.
kidsaint: The holy women at the tomb

Some women who loved Jesus went to his tomb on Easter morning. They were the first to hear that he was alive, and Jesus met them on the road. They ran to tell the apostles. Lesson: good news is for sharing!
2027-03-29.special: Monday within the Octave of Easter (solemnity): Gloria; the Easter Sequence may be sung; double Alleluia at the dismissal.
term: From the Latin for “eighth”: an eight-day celebration of a great feast. Today only Easter and Christmas have octaves in the Roman calendar. The Easter Octave ends on the Second Sunday of Easter.

family.explain: The women ran from the tomb, a little scared and very happy. Suddenly Jesus was there! He said hello, and they held his feet and worshipped him. Jesus said: Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers.
family.intention: We pray for people who are afraid, that Jesus may give them his peace.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we tell today that Jesus is alive? How will we tell them?”

illus: A teenage boy from a parish in Ernakulam was teased at college for going to Mass on Easter Monday, a holiday. A friend asked him half-mockingly: do you really believe a dead man came back? He answered: I believe because of my grandmother. She buried two children and her husband, and every Easter she still sings louder than anyone. Something real must have happened for that. The friend came with him the next Sunday.

pm.open: Risen Lord, you met the women on the road. Meet us now, and take away our fear. Alleluia. Amen.
share: It was impossible for him to be held in its power (Acts 2:24). What power of death do I fear that Christ has already broken?
They left the tomb quickly with fear and great joy (Matthew 28:8). Do I feel both fear and joy in my faith?
Go and tell my brothers (Matthew 28:10). Which brother or sister is waiting to hear from me?
pm.resp: Keep me safe, O God; you are my hope.
interc: For the newly baptized, that they may hold fast to the faith they have received.
For preachers and catechists, that they may proclaim the Resurrection with boldness.
For those who explain away the faith, that they may meet the living Lord.
For those who live in fear, that they may hear Jesus say: do not be afraid.
For our group, that we may run with the good news to those around us.
pm.close: Father, you freed your Son from death. Free us from fear and make us witnesses of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the Church keeps Easter for eight whole days, because one day is not enough for so great a joy. Today Peter stands before a great crowd and says: this Jesus God raised up, and of that all of us are witnesses (Acts 2:32).

Think of who is speaking. A few weeks earlier Peter denied Jesus three times. Now he speaks with boldness before thousands. What changed him? He met the risen Lord, and he received the Holy Spirit. The best proof of the Resurrection is a changed life.

Peter quotes David: you do not give me up to Sheol, or let your faithful one see the Pit (Psalm 16:10). David died and his tomb was still there. But Jesus' body did not see corruption. God raised him up, because it was impossible for him to be held in death's power (Acts 2:24).

In the Gospel the women run from the tomb with fear and great joy. And suddenly Jesus meets them: greetings! They hold his feet and worship him. He says: do not be afraid; go and tell my brothers. He calls those who ran away his brothers. Easter is forgiveness.

Some tried to explain it away: the disciples stole the body while we were asleep. St Augustine laughed: if they were asleep, how did they see? People still try to explain away the Resurrection. But the truth cannot be bought.
This week, let us be like the women: running with joy, holding fast to the Lord in the Eucharist, and telling our brothers and sisters: do not be afraid, he is risen. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, the women ran from the tomb so happy, and Jesus met them on the way and said: hello! Do not be afraid!
Jesus says the same to you today: do not be afraid, I am alive and I am with you. Go and tell your friends!
